headword: サービス{出勤|しゅっきん}
gloss: working without pay; unpaid attendance at work; coming to work on a day off without compensation

definitions.gloss: working without pay; unpaid attendance at work; coming to work on a day off without compensation

examples.japanese: サービス{出勤|しゅっきん}を{強|し}いられた。
examples.english: I was forced to work without pay.

examples.japanese: {休日|きゅうじつ}のサービス{出勤|しゅっきん}は{労働基準法|ろうどうきじゅんほう}{違反|いはん}になる。
examples.english: Working on a day off without pay is a violation of the Labor Standards Act.

examples.japanese: {以前|いぜん}はサービス{出勤|しゅっきん}が{当|あ}たり{前|まえ}だったが、{最近|さいきん}は{社会問題|しゃかいもんだい}として{意識|いしき}されるようになった。
examples.english: In the past, working without pay was taken for granted, but recently it has come to be recognized as a social problem.

notes:
A compound of サービス (here meaning "free of charge" or "complimentary") + {出勤|しゅっきん} (going to work). Part of a family of サービス + work terms that describe unpaid labor.

RELATED WORDS:
- サービス{残業|ざんぎょう}: unpaid overtime — working extra hours without overtime pay (the more widely known term)
- サービス{出勤|しゅっきん}: specifically refers to coming in to work on a day off without compensation

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- サービス{出勤|しゅっきん}を{強|し}いる: to force unpaid work attendance
- サービス{出勤|しゅっきん}を{断|ことわ}る: to refuse to work without pay
- サービス{出勤|しゅっきん}が{常態化|じょうたいか}する: unpaid work attendance becomes the norm

CULTURAL NOTE:
サービス{出勤|しゅっきん} and サービス{残業|ざんぎょう} reflect deep-rooted issues in Japanese work culture. While legally prohibited, social pressure and workplace norms historically made it difficult for employees to refuse. Government reforms and changing attitudes have brought increased scrutiny to these practices.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- サービス{残業|ざんぎょう}: unpaid overtime — the more commonly discussed practice
- {休日出勤|きゅうじつしゅっきん}: working on a day off — neutral term that may or may not be compensated
- ブラック{企業|きぎょう}: exploitative company — a company known for such practices
